properties.name: ROOT CAUSE (walked, measured): flo2's "853 edges gained a field on import" is an OLDER binary (the 0.59.0 release this box's launcher serves) importing a NEWER document and injecting the old schema default `role: author` onto all 853 AUTHORED_BY edges that #505's shape leaves without it — version skew, not an export leaving a default implicit; the new binary round-trips the same document with zero changes, and nothing on import compares the document's version with the binary's
properties.statement:
RUN AS THE SKILL on Anthony's "/root-cause the 853", 2026-09-14, on fact:field-confirmation-flo2-853-authored-by-edges-gained-roles-on-import-the-roles-migration-seen-from-the-consumer-side — whose own first reading (the roles migration) this walk REFUTES.

① OBSERVED, flo2's words: "Import materialises schema defaults the export left implicit — 853 of reflow2's 26,795 edges gained a field. Nothing lost, and it converges after exactly one pass. The first export after a rehydrate differs from the last one before it with zero user activity. A CI design gate comparing hashes fires falsely once per rehydrate." Expected: a rehydrate from a document and the next export are the same document, or the gate says why not. NOT affected: nodes (0 changed), every other edge type.

② PRECEDENT: fact:defect-import-materialises-defaults-so-a-restored-graph-reads-as-changed (2026-08-15, Artifact defaults — settled by removing them from the schema), fact:export-import-export-is-lossless-but-not-a-fixed-point-until-one-normalising-pass (2026-08-24, REALIZES.conformance), fact:defect-export-graph-stamps-confidently-while-the-server-reports-itself-stale (2026-09-06, fixed: a stale server refuses to export), fact:a-fresh-server-on-an-old-build-is-not-stale-and-stamps-confidently (2026-08-13), cap:a-session-serves-a-release-binary (the launcher serves target/release and rebuilds only on the builder's word).

③ CANDIDATES from the bones: (a) CHANGE — the #505 roles migration rewriting legacy AUTHORED_BY edges on import (the field-confirmation's reading). (b) CONTRACT — a schema default still injected at write for some edge property (the 08-24 class). (c) IMPLEMENTATION/VERSION SKEW — the importing binary is OLDER than the document and applies a default the newer schema dropped. (d) the exporter omitting a field the store holds. (e) OBSERVATION WRONG — the 853 is a coincidence with reflow2's AUTHORED_BY count.

④/⑤ MEASURED, 2026-09-14, reflow2-mcp CLI end to end (--import into an empty store, --diff against the document):
M1 — the export from just before #505 (12c8150: 26,637 edges, 842 AUTHORED_BY all carrying `role`) imported by the CURRENT debug binary: edges_changed 842, all AUTHORED_BY, role→roles and acted_at→authored_at/approved_at/reviewed_at. The migration, correct, one pass — and 842, not 853. (a) REFUTED as the source of the number.
M2 — the current main export (fe36d74: 26,784 edges, 853 AUTHORED_BY all carrying `roles`) imported by the CURRENT binary: design_changed 0, edges_changed 0. A fixed point. (b) and (d) REFUTED for reflow2's own document: no committed schema default remains (0 declared on nodes or edges), and reflow2's document IS in its importer's normal form.
M3 — the SAME current export imported by target/release/reflow2-mcp 0.59.0 — the binary this box's launcher serves to every session, flo2's included — then diffed: edges_changed 853, all AUTHORED_BY, every one gaining `role: author` (base null → other "author"). (c) CONFIRMED. The number is exact and the field is the old one. No committed main export has 26,795 edges; flo2's document was a working-tree export a few edges ahead of main, with the same 853.
(e) REFUTED by M3: the match is the mechanism, not a coincidence.
And import prints no warning: the document carries a stamp with the writing version and the edge vocabulary, and import_graph never compares it with the binary's own.

⑥ THE CLASS: two binaries of different schema generations sharing one document, with the older one silently rewriting the newer shape into its own. It is the mirror of the 2026-09-06 defect (an old server EXPORTING confidently) — that side now refuses; this side, an old binary IMPORTING a newer document, still does not. On this box the launcher serves the release binary and rebuilds it only on the builder's word, so every merge that changes a stored shape (#505 did) leaves every session here running older code against newer documents until someone rebuilds — and "converges after one pass" is each binary converging to ITS shape, a ping-pong between two normal forms rather than a fixed point. Would fixing this have stopped the 08-15 and 08-24 reports? No: those were same-binary, real defaults, and are settled. Would it have stopped this one? Yes, either leg: a refusal or a loud report at import names the skew instead of a phantom diff.

⑧ THE FIX AT THE CAUSE, proposed and NOT built here (Anthony's call, because one leg refuses): (1) import_graph and --import compare the document's stamp with the binary: a document written by a NEWER reflow2 (or carrying an edge vocabulary this binary lacks) is refused with the versions named and the remedy (rebuild or upgrade the server, or pass an explicit override), the same posture as the stale-export refusal; (2) an OLDER document is imported and the report SAYS what was migrated — count by edge type and property — so a diff with zero user activity is explained by the record that caused it; (3) the launcher's staleness: served_by.stale reads false for a release binary that is simply older than the code, which is the 08-13 finding and is what let this happen on the maintainer's own box. (2) is what flo2 asked for by another name; (1) is the missing refusal.

⑨ NOT ESTABLISHED: which binary flo2's session actually ran (inferred from the launcher on this box; the 0.59.0 test reproduces the number exactly); which gate fired for them (reflow2_check's behind/lineage check, or a hash comparison of their own); whether any consumer besides this box has a document ahead of its binary.
